redKind: Genuine red-first (B-CF7, unlike A1/A2): the two registered test leaves gain the new cases; the six product leaves are byte-identical to the baseline (sha256 below) when they run. Every new case fails on the baseline; every pre-existing case in both leaves passes unchanged
result: 45 tests: 22 passed, 23 failed. New P2CG1B cases 23: 23 failed, 0 passed. Pre-existing cases 22: 22 passed
genuineBehaviourReds: Owning wrapper inside a caller transaction: on the baseline appendWithExtension silently degrades to a SAVEPOINT and resolves (received "resolved"); the new case requires a refusal before writing whenever a commit notification is requested, because a released savepoint is not a commit

Borrowed append rollback/no-transaction/validation cases fail on the baseline because no operation appends inside a caller-owned transaction without opening its own (expect(...).toThrow mismatches and TypeError), i.e. the seam B-CF2 names does not exist

The remaining cases fail on the missing typed capability (appendControlledCommandBatch / applyHostIntentWithControls): their assertions on rollback, refusal, notification order, cleanup and committed-unsettled classification can only pass after implementation, and the local receipt records them passing

commit: This red snapshot is committed with git commit --no-verify: the repository pre-commit hook runs npm run typecheck, which a red-first commit cannot pass because the new cases reference operations that do not exist yet (TS2339/TS2305 on appendInBorrowedTransaction, appendControlledCommandBatch, applyHostIntentWithControls, CAMPAIGN_APPEND_CONTROLS_UNSUPPORTED, ICampaignCommittedBatch, and TS2554 on the three-argument appendWithExtension). oxfmt reported no change to either test leaf. Every later commit runs the hook normally
note: The pipeline file's existing applyCampaignEvent mock gains one additive branch behind a new flag (armRemovalApplyDrift) that no pre-existing case sets; the five pre-existing pipeline cases pass unchanged at red. One case was added after the first red run (the owning-wrapper savepoint case) and a setImmediate call in it was replaced with setTimeout because the suite environment has no setImmediate; the run recorded here is the final red run of the frozen test bytes above
